title: 'We are devastated': Family issues statement after SIU clears police in death of Clive Mensah
article: The family of Clive Mensah and their legal representatives at Kastner Lam LLP have issued a four-page press release in response to the decision that no Peel police officers will be facing charges in the death of Mississauga man Clive Mensah.
The decision brought by the province's Special Investigations Unit (SIU) was announced on March 29, more than a year after 30-year-old Mensah died.
"We are devastated. No family should have to lose a loved one this way. Clive was alone and scared and had done nothing wrong," said the family.
According to the SIU, officers were called to Mensah's Mississauga home following reports of a noise complaint on the evening of Nov. 20, 2019.

During the interaction with police, three Tasers were deployed multiple times while attempts were made to take Mensah into custody. Pepper spray was also deployed to the back of his head while he was on the ground, according to the SIU report.
The release said Mensah complied with all police orders, including returning home when he was seen wandering the neighbourhood and to lay on the ground when ordered.
Once Mensah was restrained, three responding officers left him lying face down on the ground where he became "quiet and still." Mensah eventually died in this position.

"Clive repeatedly complied with police instructions. When an officer told him to go home, he went home. The same officer followed him home and ordered him to the ground, and so he laid down. He posed no threat to any officer or any person," read the release.
The release also highlights the SIU's questions surrounding the use of multiple Tasers and pepper spray, saying it could have been better to "physically take control" before resorting to weapons.

The lack of a medical check after using significant force against Mensah, the failure to de-escalate the situation and the decision to not consider race a factor in the death are also noted in the release.

"The SIU report does not include any analysis of race as a factor in the officers' assumptions and choices. What role did Clive's identity and presentation as a young Black man play in the decisions made by Peel officers? Why was Clive seen and treated as a threat?" the family asked.
Mensah had a known history of mental illness and was suffering from schizophrenia, for which he was taking medication.

"We have waited for more than a year for the SIU to finish its investigation. In all this time, we have heard nothing from Peel Police. No explanation and no apology about what happened to Clive. And now, we see no one will be held accountable," said the family.
Peel police did issue a statement after the SIU's decision was announced, calling Mensah's death a "tragedy" and offering condolences to his family.

"Due to the unpredictable nature of policing on the front line, our officers often find themselves in difficult situations. Despite their best intentions to navigate these situations safely, there is at times a tragic outcome. We are committed to seeking collaborative opportunities to mitigate risk for persons in crisis," said Peel Regional Police Chief Nishan Duraiappah.
